title: Opening principle 1: the center
summary: Put pawns and pieces where they control e4, d4, e5 and d5.
body:
The four center squares are the crossroads of the board. Pieces there reach both wings; pieces on the rim do little.

- Start with a **center pawn** (e4 or d4; as Black, meet it with e5, d5, c5 or e6/c6).
- **Strike back** if your opponent grabs the center alone.
- Avoid early flank pawn moves (a3, h3, g4) that don't fight for the center.

examples.prompt: The first move. Claim the center.
examples.explain: 1.e4 and 1.d4 put a pawn in the center and open lines for the queen and a bishop. 1.c4 and 1.Nf3 fight for the center from the side.

examples.prompt: Black to move after 1.e4. Contest the center.
examples.explain: 1...e5 claims an equal share. c5 (Sicilian), e6 (French), c6 (Caro-Kann) and d5 all challenge e4 directly or prepare to.

examples.prompt: White to move. Keep building on the center.
examples.explain: Bc4 and Bb5 develop while eyeing the center; d4 strikes it at once; Nc3 adds another defender of e4.
